subject: science
prompt_en: Predict first: will curd set faster in a warm place or in a cool place? Tell me why you think so.
prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: dahi garam jagah pe jaldi jamega ya thandi jagah pe? Aur kyon lagta hai aisa?
answer: In the warm place; the tiny living things (bacteria) in the starter curd that turn milk into curd work faster in warmth, which is why curd takes longer to set in winter.

subject: science
prompt_en: Meena puts one ice cube on a steel plate and wraps another ice cube in a woollen shawl. Predict which one will melt first.
prompt_hi: Meena ek ice cube steel ki plate pe rakhti hai aur doosra ek woollen shawl mein lapet deti hai. Guess karo, kaunsa pehle pighlega?
answer: The ice on the plate melts first. Wool does not make heat; it slows the room's warmth from reaching the ice, so the wrapped ice melts more slowly.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said curd sets faster in a warm place. How do you know? What is actually happening in the milk?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha garam jagah pe dahi jaldi jamta hai. Ye kaise pata? Doodh ke andar asal mein ho kya raha hai?
answer: The starter curd contains tiny living things (bacteria) that grow in the milk and turn it into curd; they grow and work faster when it is warm.

subject: science
prompt_en: Meena had predicted the wrapped ice would melt first, but it melted last. Why is her test still good science?
prompt_hi: Meena ne socha tha ki shawl wali ice pehle pighlegi, par woh sabse baad mein pighli. Phir bhi uska test achhi science kyon hai?
answer: Because the test showed what really happens; a wrong prediction teaches us something new (wool slows heat) and leads to a new question. Science checks ideas instead of assuming them.

subject: science
prompt_en: Which question is testable: (A) 'Is mango the tastiest fruit?' or (B) 'Do mangoes ripen faster wrapped in newspaper or left in the open?' What makes the other one different?
prompt_hi: Kaunsa sawaal test kiya ja sakta hai: (A) 'Kya aam sabse tasty fruit hai?' ya (B) 'Kya aam newspaper mein lapetne se jaldi pakte hain ya khule mein rakhne se?' Doosra wala alag kyon hai?
answer: B is testable: we can wrap some mangoes, leave others open and watch which ripen first. A is an opinion; people can disagree and no test can settle it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Rohan notices his tulsi plant leans towards the window. Using the steps of science, what question can he ask, what might he predict, and how could he test it?
prompt_hi: Rohan dekhta hai ki uska tulsi ka paudha khidki ki taraf jhuk raha hai. Science ke steps se batao: woh kya sawaal pooch sakta hai, kya guess kar sakta hai, aur test kaise karega?
answer: Question: does the plant bend towards light? Prediction: yes, it grows towards light. Test: turn the pot around so the plant leans away from the window and watch for a few days; it bends towards the window again.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your mother says jaggery (gur) becomes soft and sticky in the rainy season. How could you check, like a scientist, whether damp air is the reason?
prompt_hi: Mummy kehti hain ki baarish ke mausam mein gur naram aur chipchipa ho jaata hai. Scientist ki tarah kaise check karoge ki kya nami wali hawa iski wajah hai?
answer: Take two similar pieces of jaggery; keep one in a closed dry jar and one in an open bowl in the same room for a few days; only the damp air differs. If only the open piece becomes sticky, damp air is the likely reason.

subject: science
prompt_en: A scientist's way of finding out starts when you first notice something. Put these steps in order, starting from noticing, and draw them as a circle: test, predict, ask a question, conclude, observe (notice something).
prompt_hi: Science mein pata lagana tab shuru hota hai jab tum pehli baar kuch notice karte ho. Noticing se shuru karke in steps ko sahi order mein lagao aur ek circle mein draw karo: test, predict, sawaal poochho, conclude, observe (kuch notice karo).
answer: Observe → ask a question → predict → test → conclude → (new question, back to observing). It is a circle because each answer leads to new questions.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'I predicted the curd would set in the fridge. It didn't, so I'll write in my notebook that I predicted it wouldn't.' What is wrong with this?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mera guess tha ki fridge mein dahi jam jaayega. Nahi jama, toh main notebook mein likh doonga ki mera guess tha ki nahi jamega.' Isme galti kya hai?
answer: A prediction must be written before the test and never changed afterwards; changing it hides what he learned. A wrong prediction is useful information.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your younger cousin thinks science means memorising answers. Explain to her how a scientist finds something out, using the curd example.
prompt_hi: Tumhari chhoti cousin sochti hai ki science matlab answers ratna. Use dahi wale example se samjhao ki scientist kaise koi baat pata karta hai.
answer: Key ideas: notice something (curd sets slowly in winter), ask a testable question, predict with a reason, test fairly (two bowls, warm and cool, same milk and starter, same time), observe and record, conclude, and ask the next question.

subject: science
prompt_en: From our last lesson, without looking back: what is the difference between a random guess and a prediction in science?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar ki baat, bina dekhe batao: science mein random guess aur prediction mein kya farak hai?
answer: A prediction is a guess with a reason, based on what you already know, made before testing; a random guess has no reason behind it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Before starting, Riya writes: 'I think the bowl in the warm place will set first.' Which step of science is this?
prompt_hi: Shuru karne se pehle Riya likhti hai: 'Mujhe lagta hai garam jagah wala katora pehle jamega.' Ye science ka kaunsa step hai?
answer: Making a prediction.

subject: science
prompt_en: In the cloth-drying test, what is the one thing you change? Name two things you keep the same.
prompt_hi: Kapda sukhane wale test mein kaunsi ek cheez badalte ho? Do cheezein batao jo same rakhte ho.
answer: Change only the type of cloth. Keep the same (any two): size of the cloth, amount of water, place and sunlight, time of hanging.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: the same wet hanky is hung once spread open and once folded into four, in the same place. Which way will it dry faster?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: wahi geela rumaal ek baar khol ke failaya, ek baar chaar tah karke, same jagah pe. Kaise jaldi sookhega?
answer: Spread open; more of the cloth is open to the air, so the water evaporates faster. Only the folding changed, so this is a fair test.

subject: science
prompt_en: Asha hangs cotton in the sun and nylon in the shade, and the cotton dries first. Before she decides, predict: can she say cotton dries faster than nylon?
prompt_hi: Asha cotton dhoop mein aur nylon chhaon mein taangti hai, aur cotton pehle sookhta hai. Socho: kya woh keh sakti hai ki cotton nylon se jaldi sookhta hai?
answer: No. Two things changed (cloth type and sun or shade), so the cotton may have dried first because of the sun. The test is unfair.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why must we change only one thing at a time in a fair test?
prompt_hi: Fair test mein ek baar mein sirf ek hi cheez kyon badalte hain?
answer: So that if the result changes, we know it was caused by that one thing; if many things change, we cannot tell which one caused it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Plan A: three same-size cloths, same water, hung together in the sun. Plan B: three different-size cloths, one in sun, one in shade, one under a fan. Which plan fairly tests the type of cloth, and what makes the other unfair?
prompt_hi: Plan A: 3 same size ke kapde, same paani, saath mein dhoop mein. Plan B: 3 alag size ke kapde, ek dhoop, ek chhaon, ek pankhe ke neeche. Kaunsa plan kapde ke type ka fair test hai, aur doosra unfair kyon hai?
answer: Plan A is fair. Plan B changes the size and the place as well as the cloth type, so we can't tell what caused any difference.

subject: science
prompt_en: Kabir's record says: 'Cotton - fast. Nylon - good. Wool - I don't like it.' What is wrong with this record?
prompt_hi: Kabir ki notebook mein likha hai: 'Cotton - fast. Nylon - achha. Wool - mujhe pasand nahi.' Is record mein kya gadbad hai?
answer: These are opinions and vague words, not observations; he should record a measurement for each cloth, such as time taken to dry in minutes, under clear headings.

subject: science
prompt_en: You want to find out whether a cricket ball bounces higher on a concrete floor or on grass. How do you make it a fair test?
prompt_hi: Tum jaanna chahte ho ki cricket ball cement ke farsh pe zyada uchhalti hai ya ghaas pe. Ise fair test kaise banaoge?
answer: Use the same ball, drop it (don't throw it) from the same height each time, measure the bounce height on each surface, change only the surface, and repeat a few times.

subject: science
prompt_en: A farmer says his new fertiliser made his wheat grow taller this year. But this year also had more rain. Can he be sure? How could he test it fairly?
prompt_hi: Ek kisaan kehta hai ki naye khaad se iss saal uska gehun lamba hua. Par iss saal baarish bhi zyada hui. Kya woh pakka keh sakta hai? Fair test kaise karega?
answer: He can't be sure, because two things changed (fertiliser and rain). Fair test: two similar plots in the same field, same seeds, same water and care in the same season, fertiliser on only one plot; then compare.

subject: science
prompt_en: Riya's notes say: 'The cotton hanky dried in 30 minutes, the nylon one in 20 minutes, and the woollen one took 50 minutes.' Put this in a table and tell me which dried fastest.
prompt_hi: Riya ke notes: 'Cotton rumaal 30 minute mein sookha, nylon 20 minute mein, aur woollen wala 50 minute mein.' Ise table mein likho aur batao sabse jaldi kaunsa sookha.
answer: Table: Cloth | Time to dry (min): Cotton 30, Nylon 20, Wool 50. Nylon dried fastest.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do scientists repeat a test instead of doing it just once?
prompt_hi: Scientist ek test sirf ek baar karne ki jagah baar-baar kyon karte hain?
answer: One result can be a mistake or happen by chance; repeating checks that the result stays the same, so it can be trusted.

subject: science
prompt_en: Teach your friend how to plan a fair test to find which soap makes the most foam. Tell her what to change, what to keep the same and what to record.
prompt_hi: Apni dost ko sikhao ki kaunsa sabun sabse zyada jhaag banata hai, iska fair test kaise plan kare. Batao kya badalna hai, kya same rakhna hai aur kya likhna hai.
answer: Change only the type of soap. Keep the same: amount of soap, amount of water, same bottle, same number of shakes. Record the height of the foam (in cm) for each soap in a table, and repeat.

subject: science
prompt_en: From our last lesson: in a fair test, how many things do we change on purpose at a time?
prompt_hi: Pichhle lesson se: fair test mein ek baar mein jaan-boojh kar kitni cheezein badalte hain?
answer: Only one; everything else is kept the same.

subject: science
prompt_en: Sort these into herb, shrub or tree: mint, rose, mango, wheat, hibiscus (gudhal), neem.
prompt_hi: In paudhon ko herb, shrub aur tree mein baanto: pudina, gulab, aam, gehun, gudhal, neem.
answer: Herbs: mint, wheat. Shrubs: rose, hibiscus. Trees: mango, neem.

subject: science
prompt_en: A mango seed sprouts in your garden. When the sapling is only knee-high, predict: is it a herb or a tree? How did you decide?
prompt_hi: Bageeche mein aam ki guthli se paudha nikla. Jab woh sirf ghutne tak ka hai, guess karo: ye herb hai ya tree? Kaise decide kiya?
answer: A tree, a young one: a mango plant grows one main stem that becomes a thick woody trunk; being short now does not make it a herb.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you gently try to bend a coriander (dhaniya) stem and a hibiscus branch. Which will bend more easily?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: dhaniye ka tana aur gudhal ki tehni, dono ko halke se modo. Kaun aasani se mudega?
answer: The coriander stem bends easily because it is a soft green herb stem; the hibiscus branch is hard and woody.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said a banana plant is a herb. Why is it not a tree, even though it is so tall?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha kela herb hai. Itna lamba hone par bhi ye tree kyon nahi hai?
answer: Its stem is not hard and woody; it is soft and made of leaf bases rolled tightly together. Plants are grouped by their stem, not only by height.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a rose bush and a guava tree. Both have woody stems. What is different about where their branches start?
prompt_hi: Gulab ki jhaadi aur amrood ka ped compare karo. Dono ke tane lakdi jaise hain. Daaliyan kahan se shuru hoti hain, isme kya farak hai?
answer: The rose branches out into many stems from near the base; the guava has one main trunk, and its branches start higher up.

subject: science
prompt_en: On your way to school you see a plant about as tall as you, with a hard woody stem that branches out many times right from the ground. Which group is it?
prompt_hi: School jaate hue tumhe ek paudha dikhta hai jo tumhare jitna lamba hai, tana sakht aur lakdi jaisa hai aur zameen ke paas se hi kai daaliyan nikalti hain. Ye kis group ka hai?
answer: A shrub.

subject: science
prompt_en: A farmer grows bottle gourd (lauki) and builds a frame of bamboo sticks and strings for it. Why does he do this?
prompt_hi: Ek kisaan lauki ugata hai aur uske liye baans aur rassi ka machaan banata hai. Woh aisa kyon karta hai?
answer: Lauki has a weak stem and is a climber; it climbs the frame using tendrils, so the plant gets more sunlight and the gourds hang off the ground and stay clean and don't rot.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw quick outlines of a herb, a shrub and a tree. Show how thick each stem is and where the branches start. Describe your drawings to me.
prompt_hi: Herb, shrub aur tree ki 3 chhoti drawing banao. Dikhao ki tana kitna mota hai aur daaliyan kahan se shuru hoti hain. Phir mujhe batao kya banaya.
answer: Herb: small plant with a thin green stem. Shrub: several woody stems branching from near the ground. Tree: tall, one thick woody trunk, branches starting high up.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu's chart says: 'Tall plants are trees and small plants are herbs.' Fix Golu's rule.
prompt_hi: Golu ke chart pe likha hai: 'Lambe paudhe tree hote hain aur chhote paudhe herb.' Golu ka rule theek karo.
answer: Group by the stem: soft green stem = herb; woody stems branching near the base = shrub; one thick woody trunk branching higher = tree. Height alone misleads: banana is a tall herb and a young mango is a short tree.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how to tell whether a plant is a herb, a shrub or a tree, using plants from your street.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki koi paudha herb, shrub ya tree hai, ye kaise pehchaanein. Apni gali ke paudhon ka example do.
answer: Key ideas: look at the stem first; soft green stem = herb (e.g. mint, grass); woody stems branching near the ground = shrub (e.g. rose, hibiscus); one thick woody trunk branching higher = tree (e.g. neem, mango); don't go by height alone.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what do we call plants with weak stems that spread along the ground, like watermelon or pumpkin?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kamzor tane wale paudhe jo zameen pe phailte hain, jaise tarbooz ya kaddu, unhe kya kehte hain?
answer: Creepers.

subject: science
prompt_en: A money plant in a pot gets a stick placed next to it. Predict what it will do over the next few weeks.
prompt_hi: Gamle mein money plant ke paas ek lakdi laga di. Guess karo, agle kuch hafton mein woh kya karega?
answer: It will climb up the stick, holding on with small roots from its stem, because its stem is too weak to stand up alone.

subject: science
prompt_en: What is the difference between a tap root and fibrous roots?
prompt_hi: Tap root aur fibrous roots mein kya farak hai?
answer: A tap root has one main thick root with thinner side roots; fibrous roots are many thin roots of similar size growing from the base of the stem, with no main root.

subject: science
prompt_en: Look at a wheat or grass leaf: its veins run side by side. Before we pull it out, predict what its roots will look like.
prompt_hi: Gehun ya ghaas ki patti dekho: nasein ek ke baaju ek seedhi chalti hain. Ukhaadne se pehle guess karo, jadein kaisi hongi?
answer: Fibrous roots: a bunch of thin, similar roots.

subject: science
prompt_en: A coriander (dhaniya) leaf has net-like veins. Predict its root type, then check a coriander bunch from the market; it often comes with roots!
prompt_hi: Dhaniye ki patti mein jaal jaisi nasein hoti hain. Jad ka type guess karo, phir bazaar ki dhaniya ki gaddi dekho, aksar jad saath aati hai!
answer: A tap root: one main root with thin side roots.

subject: science
prompt_en: You correctly said the grass will have fibrous roots. How did you know without digging it up?
prompt_hi: Tumne sahi kaha ki ghaas ki jadein fibrous hongi. Bina khode kaise pata chala?
answer: Its leaves have parallel venation, and plants with parallel venation usually have fibrous roots.
